subject: Literacy
title: Show what we know again
objectives: Children will show Term 2 learning through play stations.
Teachers will gather evidence for every child’s Term 2 record.
content: Revising rhyme and syllables, marks and fingers, and vocabulary and stories through play stations and gathering Term 2 evidence.
teachingActivities: Keep every activity familiar and playful; observe quietly and record without interrupting; offer help only when a child is stuck; celebrate what each child can do.
learnerActivities: Show what they know about rhymes, beats, marks, words and stories through play.
assessment: Observe and record each child’s Term 2 literacy learning using the four-level scale.
expectedOutcomes: Completes familiar tasks with growing independence.
Each child has an observation record for Term 2.
crossCurricular: Understanding the World: market and print

lessons.title: Revising rhyme and beats
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will revisit rhyming pairs and clapping the beats in names and words.
successCriteria: Claps the beats in their name
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have worked on rhymes, beats, fingers, marks, vocabulary, songs, stories, questions and print this term.
lessons.starter: Say "cat, hat" and clap. Say "Today we play our favourite rhyme and clap games."
teacherActivities: Play finish the rhyme with the cat and hat cards.
Clap the beats in names around the circle.
Play rhyme lotto with the six cards.
Let each child choose a game.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play finish the rhyme with the cat and hat cards. Children: Children say the rhyming word.
Step 2. Teacher: Clap the beats in names around the circle. Children: Children clap their names.
Step 3. Teacher: Play rhyme lotto with the six cards. Children: Children match pairs.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a game. Children: Child chooses and plays.

practical.title: Rhyme and clap games
steps: Children play rhyme lotto and name claps.
The teacher notes who finishes rhymes and claps beats.
practical.safety: Keep clapping gentle and supervise turn-taking. Clear the floor.

differentiation.support: Play with the child and use two pairs only.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to teach a friend a rhyme game.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.homeConnection: Say rhyming pairs and clap names at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit rhyming pairs and clapping the beats in names and words" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Revising marks and fingers
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will revisit squeezing, threading and mark-making.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have worked on rhymes, beats, fingers, marks, vocabulary, songs, stories, questions and print this term.
lessons.starter: Wiggle your fingers and say "Today our fingers play and make marks."
teacherActivities: Set up playdough and bead threading tables.
Set up crayons and sand for marks.
Walk round and ask "What did you make?"
Let each child choose a favourite activity.
learnerActivities: Children make marks and say a word.
Child shows and names their work.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up playdough and bead threading tables. Children: Children squeeze, roll and thread.
Step 2. Teacher: Set up crayons and sand for marks. Children: Children make marks and say a word.
Step 3. Teacher: Walk round and ask "What did you make?" Children: Child shows and names their work.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a favourite activity. Children: Child chooses and plays.

practical.title: Fingers and marks
steps: Set up four tables with different materials.
The teacher notes how each child holds and uses tools.
practical.safety: Supervise beads and water closely. Use non-toxic dough and crayons and wash hands after.

differentiation.support: Work beside the child with one material.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a pattern with beads or marks.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Makes marks and says what they show
lessons.conclusion: Wash hands and say goodbye to the materials.
lessons.homeConnection: Let your child play with dough and crayons at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit squeezing, threading and mark-making" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Revising words and stories
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will revisit market words, songs, stories and questions.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have worked on rhymes, beats, fingers, marks, vocabulary, songs, stories, questions and print this term.
lessons.starter: Say "Good morning, ma" and say "Today we visit the market and hear a story."
teacherActivities: Play at the market stall with polite words.
Tell the little hen story with the story box.
Ask who, what and where questions about the story.
Find name cards and say whose they are.
learnerActivities: Children ask for items with please.
Children answer with words or gestures.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play at the market stall with polite words. Children: Children ask for items with please.
Step 2. Teacher: Tell the little hen story with the story box. Children: Children join in and retell.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask who, what and where questions about the story. Children: Children answer with words or gestures.
Step 4. Teacher: Find name cards and say whose they are. Children: Child finds their card.

practical.title: Market and story
steps: Set up the market stall and the story box.
The teacher notes words and story retelling.
practical.safety: Supervise each space and keep floors clear. Use toy foods and large props.

differentiation.support: Offer two choices and say the words with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to be the seller or the storyteller.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Close the market and say "The end."
lessons.homeConnection: Tell stories and play shop at home with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit market words, songs, stories and questions" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Play stations again
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will gather evidence of each child’s Term 2 literacy learning at play stations.
successCriteria: Completes familiar tasks with growing independence
Shows rhyme, speaking, print and fine motor skills
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have worked on rhymes, beats, fingers, marks, vocabulary, songs, stories, questions and print this term.
lessons.starter: Sing a favourite song and show six stations to the class.
teacherActivities: Set up six stations: rhyme, beats, fingers, marks, story and print.
Observe each child at two stations and record what they can do.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up six stations: rhyme, beats, fingers, marks, story and print. Children: Children rotate every three minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: Observe each child at two stations and record what they can do. Children: Children play at stations.
Step 3. Teacher: Take photographs and make notes. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Six stations
steps: Set up six stations with familiar materials.
practical.safety: Supervise each station with an adult or helper. Keep floors clear and materials large and soft.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and stay at familiar stations.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to show friends how a station works.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: finishes rhymes; claps beats; uses fingers; makes marks; retells a story; finds their name card.

lessons.conclusion: Say well done and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Play a favourite game from this term at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will gather evidence of each child’s Term 2 literacy learning at play stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Term 2 celebration
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will celebrate Term 2 with songs, stories and games, and teachers will complete their records.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have worked on rhymes, beats, fingers, marks, vocabulary, songs, stories, questions and print this term.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we celebrate. Let us sing our favourite songs and tell our favourite story."
teacherActivities: Tell the hen story with the props.
Give each child a sticker or praise and say their name.
learnerActivities: Children join in and choose a song.
Child waves and says thank you.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sing favourite songs with actions. Children: Children join in and choose a song.
Step 2. Teacher: Tell the hen story with the props. Children: Children retell with props.
Step 3. Teacher: Give each child a sticker or praise and say their name. Children: Child waves and says thank you.

practical.title: Celebration circle
steps: Sing, tell the story and say each name.
practical.safety: Check for allergies before any snack and use non-toxic stickers. Supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hand and sing along.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose the last song.

assessment.method: Complete each child’s Term 2 literacy record using today’s observations and the week’s notes. Record a next step for Term 3.

questions.question: Did you like the story?
questions.expected: Yes with a smile or word.

lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say "See you in Term 3."
lessons.homeConnection: Keep singing, telling stories and playing with sounds during the holiday.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "celebrate Term 2 with songs, stories and games, and teachers will complete their records" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
